answer:
Two records that happen to share a number. The CRM forces that answer rather than merely permitting it, and it also tells you where to put the clash so it is not silently erased.

1. Thing and label are separate entities. The specification is explicit that the appellation, and the relation between the appellation and the referred item, "must not be confused with the referred item and its identity" (crm732#s0044, Modelling principles > Reality, Knowledge Bases and CIDOC CRM). The fact that one string was written twice is a fact about the string, and carries no implication about how many things exist. There is no route in the CRM by which sharing an identifier makes two things one.

2. What does decide the count is the identity criterion of the things themselves. Generally: "informed people are able to agree that they refer to the same, single thing in its distinction from others" (crm732#s0065). For stratigraphic units CRMarchaeo makes this concrete and spatial — the A8 Stratigraphic Unit scope note agreed by the SIG under Issue 300 (36th meeting, Heraklion 2016) ends "the place an instance of A8 Stratigraphic Unit occupies can be uniquely identified with respect to the surrounding reference space of archaeological interest". A posthole in Trench 3 and a pit fill in Trench 7 occupy different places, result from different genesis events, and are not even the same kind of stratigraphic unit. They are two instances, unavoidably.

3. Classes for the two units. The Trench 7 pit fill is an A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit — a bounded, homogeneous portion of terrain. The Trench 3 posthole is an A3 Stratigraphic Interface if, as single-context recording normally implies, the sheet records the cut: a boundary surface left where matter was removed. CRMarchaeo's own accepted example follows exactly this convention, numbering a cut "[19]" (A3) against a deposit "(2)" (A2) (49th SIG meeting, March 2021). If the Trench 3 sheet in fact describes the fill of the posthole rather than its cut, that unit is an A2 as well. Either way the two are distinct instances of A8 Stratigraphic Unit, and in the likeliest reading they are not even in the same subclass — which is a further reason the merge reading is untenable.

4. "Record" resolves at the document, and there were always two documents. Each 1978 context sheet is an E31 Document that P70 documents its own unit. The digital archive falls under the same class — E31's scope note states "Documentation databases are regarded as instances of E31 Document" (crm732#E31). So the digitisation should carry two records forward, one per sheet/unit, not one record with two descriptions.

5. Where the clash actually lives: E15 Identifier Assignment. Do not model this only as P1 is identified by. `connect A8 E42` reports that the CRM declares P1 as a shortcut for the full path "E1 CRM Entity. P140i was attributed by (assigned attribute to): E15 Identifier Assignment. P37 assigned (was assigned by): E42 Identifier". Unfolding that shortcut is what makes the collision expressible at all:
   - one E42 Identifier, P190 has symbolic content "56";
   - E15 #1: P14 carried out by the Trench 3 supervisor, P4 has time-span 1978, P37 assigned that identifier, P140 assigned attribute to the Trench 3 unit;
   - E15 #2: the same shape, carried out by the Trench 7 supervisor, P140 assigned attribute to the Trench 7 unit.
   Assert P1 alone and you get two units bearing the same label with no record of who labelled them or when — which is precisely the evidence that the duplication was accidental rather than an assertion of sameness. (There is no dedicated subproperty of P140 for E15; P140 itself is the property to use, as Christian-Emil Ore noted on the list, t0633.)

6. The remedy is at the identifier, not at the units. E42 requires codes that "identify them uniquely and permanently within the context of one or more organisations" (crm732#E42). Bare "56" fails that test within this site's numbering series, so it cannot serve as the archive's identifier for either unit. Mint two disambiguated identifiers (site code + trench + 56) as new instances of E42 in a present-day E15 Identifier Assignment; E15's scope note provides for building an identifier from constituents, recorded with P142 used constituent. If the archive wants to state that bare "56" is no longer to be used, the same E15 can carry P38 deassigned — the redrafted P38 scope note approved as Issue 630 (57th SIG meeting, Marseille 2023) says "de-assignment may be associated with the assignment of a new identifier" in the same instance of E15. Crucially, keep the two 1978 assignments in the record: they are the historical fact, and they are how a future user understands why two units in the archive both answer to "56".

7. One point the CRM has genuinely not settled: whether the "56" on the two sheets is one instance of E42 or two. In Issue 383 Robert Sanderson argued that "if the same string was used by different Symbolic Objects, then it seems like they would actually be the same symbolic object"; Martin Doerr replied "This is a long debated question", noting cases where the identity of an E90 is bound to the sender. The issue was closed without resolving it. Practically, a single E42 "56" with two E15 assignments makes the clash queryable in one hop and is what I would recommend; two scope-qualified identifiers make each unit self-describing. Neither choice disturbs the answer: two units, two assignment events, two records.

What not to do: do not create one merged entity for "context 56". CRMarchaeo already has the class for legitimately declaring that separate stratigraphic units are remains of one original thing — A6 Group Declaration Event — and it is an interpretive activity requiring evidence of shared origin. Nothing of the kind is present here; the geography rules it out. Using it, or informally collapsing the two, would encode a false archaeological claim in order to preserve a clerical accident.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: This is the class for the interpretive act of declaring that two or more stratigraphic units are the remains of one original physical thing. It is exactly the tempting move here ("context 56 is one thing in two pieces") and exactly the wrong one: it requires an evidenced archaeological judgement of shared origin, and a posthole in Trench 3 and a pit fill in Trench 7 have none. Using it would turn a clerical accident into a false interpretation.

A reading of "context" as the unit of excavation rather than the unit of stratification. A1 is the activity of progressively recording and removing matter; it is a process, not the deposit or surface that the context sheets describe. The number on the sheet labels the observed unit, so the referent is an A8 Stratigraphic Unit. (If the 1978 site had numbered spits rather than contexts the analysis would shift to A1, but the sheets name a posthole and a pit fill.)

The other subclass of S20 in CRMarchaeo, and a real trap for a cut context: A10 is the surface produced by the excavation itself, which merely "would have the intention to approximate an instance of A3 Stratigraphic Interface". The Trench 3 posthole cut is an archaeological interface that existed before 1978, not an artefact of the trowelling, so A3 is correct and A10 is not.

Considered as a way of relating the two "56"s. It relates appellations regarded as equivalent regardless of the thing denoted, i.e. variant forms of one name. The two occurrences here are the same form, not variants, and the problem is that they denote different things — the opposite of what P139 asserts.

Usable — the SIG voted to keep it under Issue 519 (closed Marseille 2023) — but its own scope note says preferred status "can be better expressed in a context independent form" by typing the E15 Identifier Assignment with P2 has type. Since this case already needs the E15 events unfolded to carry the clash, designating preference on those events is the more economical route, so I route through E15/P2 rather than P48.

siblings_considered.why_not: A7 is the other subclass of A8 that covers volumes, but it is specifically for documenting matter that holds one or more physical things in a stable position within a surrounding A2. The Trench 7 sheet records the fill as a deposit in its own right, not as the embedding of a find; if finds are later related to it, they attach via A7 in addition, not instead.

This is the sibling a knowledgeable reader would press on, since it is the class I used for the other "56". A2 is a bounded volume of deposit; a posthole cut is a coherent part of a boundary surface marking where the effect of a removal event ended, which is A3. I flag the dependency openly: if the Trench 3 sheet turns out to record the posthole's fill rather than its cut, A2 is right for it too — and the two units are still two.

The nearest sibling under E41, and not a plausible rival: "56" is a code allocated by an organisation to pick a unit out of its own numbering series, which is E42's definition, whereas E35 covers strings culturally recognisable as titles. The rival I would actually argue with is the parent E41 Appellation, which is not a sibling; E42 is preferred because the site was operating a numbering scheme intended to be unique, and that intention is what "56" broke.

E17 is the right class for the other thing on those sheets — the supervisor's determination that this unit is a posthole or a pit fill. It is not the act at issue. The clash arose in the allocation of a code from a numbering book, which is E15, and only E15 carries P37 assigned and P38 deassigned to E42.

The sheets are handwritten natural language and could also be instantiated as E33. But E33 says only that they are expressions in a language; what the archive needs is that each sheet makes propositions about a particular unit, which is E31 and its necessary property P70 documents. Multiple instantiation as E31 and E33 is available if language needs recording; E31 is the load-bearing choice.

notes: Two things the tools made awkward. (1) `concept <id>` is not a quotable source for `quote`, so scope-note wording can only be verified against the declaration chunks (crm732#E31, crm732#E42) or against the SIG minutes that agreed the text. For CRMarchaeo that matters, because the 7.3.2 declaration corpus is CRMbase only — the A8/A2/A3 scope notes are reachable through `concept`, but the only quotable attestation I could find for them is the 2016 Heraklion minutes under Issues 300, 301 and 284. (2) `docs --json` is the only way to see a chunk's full text and its chunk_id; the default output truncates at roughly one sentence, which makes narrative passages hard to weigh without it. Substantively, the one thing I could not settle from the case text is whether the Trench 3 sheet records the posthole cut or the posthole's fill; I have proposed A3 on the single-context reading and stated the A2 fallback explicitly, since the answer to the question asked is unaffected either way. I also found no SIG discussion of duplicate archaeological context numbers specifically — the nearest real precedents are the mis-assigned coin identifiers on the list (t0633) and the P38 deassignment redraft (Issue 630).
